Bugs are one thing. The ridiculous amount of bugs may be fixed over time.

But the whole design of this instalment is an all-time low in the Sniper Elite Series. That just will not be fixed in a patch, "coming soon™".

Sniper Elite 5 was a mixed bag, probably making more steps backwards compared to SE4 than forwards, but it was ultimately saved with the innovative idea of Axis Invasion. It had its flaws as well, but was all in all, tons of fun to play.
And now they made sure that even Axis Invasion is no longer fun. They took away all the options to tech for damage as the invader (no trench gun, KAR98K is a DLC...), tipping the balance ultimately towards the allied player with their legal wallha... sorry, focus ability. 
Having enough options for firepower in SE5 allowed for some nonetheless fairly balanced matches that were fun to play. 
None of this fun is present in Resistance. It's not fun as an invader, and not fun as an allied player.   

If you enjoyed Sniper Elite 5... then keep playing Sniper Elite 5, and skip this disgraceful cash-grab.

[h1]Sniper Elite: Resistance – A Buggy But Familiar Experience[/h1]

If you're a fan of the Sniper Elite series like me, you might want to hold off on this one until it's on sale—or at the very least, patched into a more polished state. Having sunk nearly 600 hours into SE5, completing every achievement, unlocking everything, and racking up over 1,200 kills in Invasion mode, I had high hopes.

[h3]Bugs Galore[/h3]
I've lost count of how many times the AI has glitched out—walking into each other and getting stuck in an endless loop of walking animations, spinning on the spot, or even spotting me through solid walls. Some ammo packs you cannot pick up, grenades stick to invisible walls, and AI can sometimes open locked doors that I still can't walk through unless I manually pick or break the lock. There are so many window openings that should be climbable but aren't, and hip-high walls that you can't vault over—something SE5 handled far better. Pathways that seem accessible, are not and if you do manage to step onto them, you risk getting soft-locked and needing to reload a save.

[h3]Game play[/h3]
The core game play remains similar to SE5, which is a plus. Despite the bugs, the maps still offer a decent challenge, whether you're trying to complete them undetected or take out every enemy methodically.

[h3]What Doesn't Work[/h3]
Harry Hawker – [i]Incredibly[/i] irritating voice and talks way too much as you play. If you're in Invasion mode, this actually works in your favour, since you can overhear him talking to himself. If you can't stand the forced gritty South London accent, swap characters to anyone but Harry.

While some bugs have been patched, there are still way too many for a game that should have spent more time in QA before release.

Weapon mods locked behind DLC – The Lights, Camera, Achtung DLC unlocks some rifle mods. Wouldn’t it have made more sense to add entirely new weapons as well?

[h3]What Works[/h3]
Bullet time is still satisfying – The signature slow-mo kill cam remains as fun as ever.
Controls stay familiar – No need to relearn everything if you've played SE5.
New challenge mode – A nice addition, even if it's a bit short. Invasion mode also makes a return.

[h3]Final Verdict[/h3]
Would I recommend this? If you're a hardcore Sniper Elite fan, maybe—but expect a rough ride. If you're on the fence, I'd suggest waiting for a sale or via Game Pass. Right now, it's just too unpolished to justify the full price. Here’s hoping the devs sort out the bugs soon.

Sniper Elite: Resistance - A Frustrating Step Backward for the Series

IMO Sniper Elite: Resistance represents a significant misstep for a franchise that once prided itself on tactical precision and immersive gameplay. What should have been a thrilling wartime stealth experience instead delivers a buggy, unpolished mess that frequently breaks player immersion and tests patience.

Technical Issues Plague Every Aspect
The game's most glaring problems stem from its technical shortcomings. NPCs regularly clip through walls and merge with environmental structures, creating unintentionally comedic moments that shatter any sense of tension. More seriously, players frequently encounter game-breaking bugs, including instances of falling through floor textures and getting stuck in invisible barriers that prevent movement. These aren't rare occurrences – they're persistent issues that plague nearly every mission.

Artificial Unintelligence
The enemy AI represents another major disappointment. NPCs display barely any tactical awareness or self-preservation instincts, often running predetermined paths regardless of nearby threats. Guard behaviors feel mechanical and predictable, lacking the dynamic responses that made previous entries challenging and engaging. The result is less a tactical shooter and more an exercise in exploiting obviously scripted behavior patterns.

Harry: The Character Nobody Asked For
Perhaps the most grating element is the new character Harry, voiced by Jason Statham in what might be his most phoned-in performance to date. While Statham's gruff delivery could have worked with better direction and writing, Harry instead becomes an irritating presence due to endlessly recycled dialogue lines. The same handful of quips and observations repeat ad nauseam, making players wish for a "mute companion" option that sadly doesn't exist without muting all other companions.

Missed Opportunities
What's particularly frustrating is glimpsing the game that could have been beneath all these issues. The core sniping mechanics remain solid when they work, and some mission environments show creative potential in their layout. However, these fleeting bright spots only serve to highlight how thoroughly the technical problems and poor execution undermine the experience.

Sound Design: A Mixed Bag
While the game's audio design generally maintains series standards for weapon effects and ambient sound, Harry's repetitive dialogue and some inconsistent mixing detract from the overall atmosphere. Footstep audio occasionally desyncs from character animations, adding to the general sense of poor polish.

Conclusion
Sniper Elite: Resistance feels like a rushed product that needed several more months of development and quality assurance testing. The fundamental gameplay loop that made the series popular still exists somewhere in this package, but it's buried under layers of technical issues, weak AI, and frustrating design choices. Series veterans and newcomers alike would be better served revisiting previous entries or waiting for a substantial patch to address the game's numerous problems.

Score: 3/10

Pros:
- Core sniping mechanics remain functional when not impacted by bugs
- Some well-designed mission environments
- Decent weapon sound effects

Cons:
- Frequent and severe technical issues
- Weak enemy AI that breaks immersion
- Repetitive and poorly delivered companion dialogue
- Numerous collision and clipping problems
- General lack of polish throughout
- Inconsistent performance even on capable hardware

Unfortunately, Rebellion is getting very lazy and greedy with Sniper Elite franchise. I don't think I will pay them more money for this franchise, unless they bring up  some real value for the money we give them.  Their current idea of creativity is releasing a game that resembles their previous game with some minor differences and milking money from their customers. This is unacceptable for me!  

1. Sniper Elite: Resistance is pretty much a polished version of Sniper Elite 5 (SE5) with very few differences.
2. After Easy Anti-cheat's disasterous experince and crashes, they still don't seem to find a better anti-cheat. I saw players who are getting out of map and killing people from there, running lightining fast, teleporting behind enemies and stab them, using unlimited ammo (flare, grenades, mines, etc to wipe out the entire map), using aim assists in multiplayer which makes no sense at all! 
3. There are very few weapons from Sniper Elite 5 in this game, although the story of the game is a sequel to SE5.  You can be German sniper on multiplayer, but you cannot use German weapons of SE5 like Gewehr. You can use Kar-98, but Rebellion thought about milking money from their customers for it. We could use it in SE5 freely, now you have to pay money for that. Being a German sniper with French weapon is stupid to say the least. 
4. I am very disappointed with Season Pass 1 as well. DLC's give no value for the money. They brought back Fairborne and SE5 multiplayer maps with a DLC? Terrible idea! I didn't pay Rebellion to give me the same content with the previous game. It is why I won't buy any more Season Passes or DLCs unless they change their vision!
5. They broke a multiplayer map in one of their updates that was all about advertising their DLC. You can no longer climb some of the ladders, but you can get down from them which is utterly nonsense. I reported it to them, they haven't fixed it for months now, which is alone unacceptable. How can you have a ladder that no one can climb on? Also, there are more bugs I've seen like invisible walls while hiding behind sand boxes, boxes. I frequently saw another annoying bug that makes you unable to perform any action after defusing or planting mines. It's seen like you are defusing a mine, but you cannot do anything. Also you can freeze in game. Sometimes some rifles or smgs cannot shoot even if you push the shoot button, they freeze too.
6. The community of the game is too much toxic. Everyone is fighting with each other. You can report people who are hostile against you, but Rebellion does absolutely nothing for them, just they don't do anything for real cheaters in game. Whenever you kill someone or a couple of players on multiplayer games, they either call you a cheater or they want to kick you, which is unacceptable too.  2-3 people can kick someone without a reason and they laugh at you. Most people abuse kick votes which is unacceptable. Rebellion should find a way for preventing this abuse. This has been a problem for ages.
7. Higher prestige levels mean only one thing: More votes for kicks. Whenever lower people see you joining a multiplayer game, they start voting for you. There is absolutely no reason to level prestige if you don't want to be kicked many times. Perks? Meh...they are useless. 

In conclusion, I'm too much disappointed with Sniper Elite:Resistance. I certainly do not recommend this game to anyone. In fact, I fail to see that this game has any more value over Sniper Elite 5, except for what? Propaganda missions? I can go back and play Sniper Elite 5 instead.

Rebellion should really get their heads back together or they are gonna get a really negative response from their customers on their next releases!
